clue.text: A cat knocking over nice grey power source

indicators.note: things knocked over are scattered out of place, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a tom is a male cat
the letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy cat topples a pleasant grey object that turns out to be a source of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic energy drives nuclear power stations, so it is literally a source of power.

clue.text: A lecturer to ponder — starter's missing salt

indicators.note: the starter is the opening letter, and it is said to be absent from the word for ponder

parts.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for lecturer
to ruminate is to think something over

explanation.surface: An academic is left to ponder why a starter course arrived without its salt.
explanation.walkthrough: RUMINATE loses its first letter R to leave UMINATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aluminate is a chemical salt containing aluminium combined with oxygen as part of the anion.

clue.text: Sketches exposed columns

parts.note: a secret that is out has been exposed
columns of soldiers or text are lines

explanation.surface: Drawings that show the bare columns of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlines are rough preliminary drawings or summaries, which is what sketches are as a noun.

clue.text: Over race, I pick up bit of cramp and suffer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the word that follows is read the other way
to pick something up is to take it into your hold, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a run is a race

indicators.note: a bit is a small piece, here just the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of cramp

explanation.surface: A runner gets cramp during a race and suffers for it.
explanation.walkthrough: RUN is turned round to NUR, C goes in after its N, and I goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it on yourself and so suffer it.

clue.text: Powerful drug, strong etc working in 5

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: one set of letters is placed inside the word for the number
something working is in operation and being reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the three letters rearranged
the number written as a word
F stands for forte, strong in music

explanation.surface: A list of a powerful drug's strong ingredients, etcetera, working in five ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 looks like a cross-reference to 5 down, but it is just the number FIVE, split open by the shuffled ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something effective produces the intended result strongly, so it is potent or powerful.

clue.text: Involve roughly 10 + 1 + 49?

indicators.note: something done roughly is not done neatly, so the letters come out in a loose new order

parts.note: the number written as a word
one is a, as in a single thing
in loose Roman numerals, I before L is one less than fifty

explanation.surface: A rough sum that adds 10, 1 and 49 together.
explanation.walkthrough: IL for 49 is not proper Roman notation (that is XLIX), which is why the clue has a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to make it a necessary consequence, so it is a synonym of involve.

clue.text: European consents to remove coat before king

indicators.note: taking off a coat strips away the outside, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: to consent is to agree
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A European agrees to take off his coat in front of the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek is a native of Greece, a country in Europe, so a Greek is one kind of European.

clue.text: Give fines during road trip

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters fall into a new order
something happening during something else sits within it

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
F stands for fine, as on pencils, so two of them

explanation.surface: Speeding motorists hand out money in fines during a road trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford can mean to provide or supply, as in a window affording a view, which is giving.

clue.text: Over £10 for an apple?

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so in this down clue the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

explanation.surface: Is ten pounds too much to pay for one apple?
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet, from French reinette, is an old name for several varieties of dessert apple, beside its cheese-making sense.

clue.text: Food group is regularly wrapped in paper

indicators.note: something wrapped in a covering sits inside it

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A category of food is routinely sold wrapped in paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food group' looks like the definition, but group is needed for the wordplay, leaving just Food.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit is an everyday type of food eaten raw or cooked.

clue.text: In America, it makes Joe eat fierce curry

indicators.note: a curry is a dish of mixed ingredients cooked together, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An American called Joe likes to eat fiery curry.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe is American slang for coffee, not a man's name; a cafetiere is a plunger coffee pot, called a French press in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafetiere brews coffee, which Americans call joe, so in America it makes joe.

clue.text: 24 down bored by current Republican actor

indicators.note: something bored by a drill has a hole made in it with something going inside

parts.note: the answer to 24 down is a colour, and olive is a shade of it
I is the symbol for electric current
R abbreviates Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican actor is bored stiff by environmental politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 down is GREEN, and OLIVE is one shade of green; I goes between its V and E, with R at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was a celebrated English stage and film actor.

clue.text: Yellow bird

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a canary; yellow is slang for cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is slang for a coward or cowardly, and is also the common farmyard fowl.

clue.text: Heard spiel about car showroom

indicators.note: about means around and turned every way, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: the ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A customer listens to the sales patter at a car showroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealership is a franchised business selling one maker's cars, typically from a showroom.

clue.text: Small tuft of hair? That's right, more than tiddly

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a quiff is a tuft of hair brushed up over the forehead
i.e. stands for id est, that is
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy fusses over a quiff in the mirror and asks if it looks right.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiddly and squiffy are both British slang for slightly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Squiffy means tipsy, so the comparative squiffier is drunker, more than merely tiddly.

clue.text: Spot of blue material

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small flake or speck of soot
second meaning: obscene or pornographic content

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a dab of blue fabric, but blue here means indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: A smut is a speck of soot or dirt, and smut is also indecent writing or pictures.

clue.text: Soldier meets elite soldiers to gather tops of trees, including small parts of logs

parts.note: a man is an ordinary soldier

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, so initials are taken

parts.note: the first letters of both words

indicators.note: to gather something is to collect it in, so letters are held between the others

parts.note: the SAS is the British Special Air Service regiment
S abbreviates small

explanation.surface: Troops in a forest collect the tops of trees and bits of logs.
explanation.walkthrough: Logs here are logarithms, not timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantissa is the fractional part of a logarithm, so mantissas are parts of logs in mathematics.

clue.text: Bound to be caught after initially slogging

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter
to be trapped is to be caught

explanation.surface: After a long slog, someone is certain to be captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to'; Bound alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped means tied with straps, so it is a synonym of bound in the sense of tied up.

clue.text: One dismissed by head cook

indicators.note: someone dismissed is sent away, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a chief is a head or leader
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One member of staff is sacked by the head cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head cook' reads as one phrase, but head is wordplay and cook is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook in a restaurant kitchen.

clue.text: Wife quietly wearing fur, treading carefully around this?

indicators.note: something wearing a garment is inside it, so these letters go within the word for fur

parts.note: an animal's fur is its coat
W abbreviates wife
P is piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: A wife in a fur coat steps very carefully across a muddy field.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowpat is a round dropping of cow dung in a field, which walkers carefully step around.

clue.text: Note wonderful fashion, I see

parts.note: super means excellent
the ton is an old word for fashionable style or society
taken as written
C sounds like see when spoken

explanation.surface: A remark that a fashion show is wonderful, as I observe.
explanation.definitionFit: The supertonic is the second degree of a musical scale, one step above the tonic, so it is a note.

clue.text: Monarch raising some plesiosaur (a sea creature)

indicators.note: raising something in a down clue lifts it upwards, so the letters read bottom to top
some means part of, so the letters sit within a longer run of text

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of plesiosaur, a, sea and the start of creature

explanation.surface: A monarch hoisting up part of a fossil plesiosaur, a prehistoric sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar became a title for Roman emperors, and so stands for any supreme ruler or monarch.

clue.text: Drunk upset by heads of shandy, each drink chucked

indicators.note: upset means knocked upside down, so in this down clue the word is flipped

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so each word's initial is taken

parts.note: the first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A drunk, annoyed at being served shandy, throws each drink away.
explanation.walkthrough: Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: Tossed means thrown casually, which is exactly chucked.

clue.text: A world-beating fine hotel

indicators.note: something given a beating is battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the six letters as written, for rearranging
F stands for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A superb hotel that beats all others in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The Waldorf Astoria in New York is a famous luxury hotel, often called simply the Waldorf.

clue.text: Lover not finished with woman's proposition

indicators.note: not means without, so a word meaning finished is taken out of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
something finished is over
Emma is a woman's name; the 's links to what follows

explanation.surface: A lover who doesn't quite finish making a proposal to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' looks like the usual signal to drop a last letter; instead OVER, meaning finished, is removed from LOVER to leave L.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a lemma is a subsidiary proposition proved to help establish a larger theorem.

clue.text: Touring end of pier eating assorted rock

indicators.note: someone touring travels inside a place, so one letter goes within the others
assorted means mixed, so the letters are mixed into a new order
the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is taken

parts.note: the last letter
the six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Day-trippers walk to the end of the pier eating assorted sticks of seaside rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Seaside rock is a stick of hard candy sold in British resorts, but here rock is the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a hard igneous rock made of quartz, feldspar and mica.

clue.text: New information surrounding 19

indicators.note: surrounding means placed all round, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
19 across is a note of the scale, and in sol-fa that degree is re

explanation.surface: Fresh information about some cross-referenced matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The supertonic is the second note of the scale, sung as re in do-re-mi.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or new to something, as in a green recruit.

clue.text: It's a crime to break truce

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it into pieces that can be put back in a new order

parts.note: the nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests that violating a ceasefire is a criminal act.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a formal agreement between warring sides to stop fighting, which is a truce.

clue.text: Old man sat cooking dish

indicators.note: cooking changes ingredients, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad sat at the stove making a dish for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is an Italian staple served as a dish, such as spaghetti or penne.

clue.text: Rickety garden shed stores North American weapons

indicators.note: a place that stores things holds them inside
something rickety is falling apart, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the ten letters rearranged
N for North and A for American

explanation.surface: A tumbledown shed in the garden is hiding weapons from North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand grenades are small explosive bombs thrown by hand, a type of weapon.
